confirmedFacts: The official March 2026 imaging calibration includes all listed standard-star programs and detector-specific PHOTMJSR values; the three Cycle 3 hot standards used here are on that official roster.

MAST returned 7,085 public observation rows across twelve Cycle 1-4 calibration programs; Program 6605 supplied the three selected hot standards and Program 7565 already exposes two new Cycle 4 hot standards for a future holdout.

Forty-eight Program 6605 CAL products were checked by precise FITS target coordinates. Twenty-four products actually contained the standard: three target-detector anchors, two filters, and four dither positions per group.

A header sample spanning all six target-filter groups was reprocessed on 2026-07-12 with JWST pipeline 2.0.1 under CRDS context jwst_1535.pmap. This cycle did not diff that build context against jwst_1490.pmap, so reference-file identity is not assumed from the serial number.
All six groups retained 4/4 support and zero DO_NOT_USE pixels inside r=3. Their r=5 robust scatter was below 1%.
WDFS0458-56 NRCB1 F090W nevertheless had a 2.308405% maximum dither excursion, and its normalized pattern differed from WDFS0122-30 by as much as 2.155367%. Both registered gates failed.
F150W passed the cross-star matched-pattern gate at 0.567413%, so the failure is not a universal property of the geometry or implementation.
Independent Node recomputation matched every Python group metric and decision exactly at the retained numeric precision.
inferences: The raw r=5 aperture operator is repeatable in a robust central sense but not sufficiently transferable to treat the sampled F090W dither signature as a fixed detector-position correction.

Because the official calibration path applies jump-step adjudication and per-image STPSF aperture corrections before comparing with CALSPEC, this failure does not falsify jwst_1490.pmap, PHOTMJSR, or Boyer et al.'s aggregate calibration result.
The failure persists from r=3 through r=8 for WDFS0458-56 F090W, so a simple increase in aperture radius is unlikely to be the sole remedy.
The divergence between F090W and F150W makes a filter-dependent PSF, jump, or exposure-state term more plausible than a target-independent four-position flat-field signature.
unverifiedProposals: On the retired RC73 development data, decompose the WDFS0458-56 F090W pattern-2 deficit with the official jump flag/no-jump branch and per-image STPSF aperture fractions; do not change RC73's verdict.
Freeze the resulting operator before opening Program 7565 WDFS1304+10 and WDFS1557+55 pixels. Use those Cycle 4 standards as the independent two-star holdout with the same dither-pattern gates.
Only if the fresh isolated-star holdout passes should a wide-position calibration design be written; only after that should a new disjoint crowded-field tile be opened.

prizeStatus.finding: No official cash prize or challenge award is attached to this calibration subproblem. The broader Hubble-tension problem has no single official solution prize recorded by this cycle.
